title: En passant
summary: Capturing a pawn that has just double-stepped past yours, only on the very next move.

steps.md:
When a pawn makes its **two-square first move** and lands right beside an enemy pawn, that enemy pawn may capture it **as if it had moved only one square**. It moves diagonally onto the square the pawn skipped. This is **en passant** ("in passing").

- Only pawn takes pawn.
- The capturing pawn must be on its 5th rank (White) or 4th rank (Black).
- It is allowed **only on the very next move**; otherwise the chance is gone.
Black has just played ...d7-d5, passing the d6-square right next to White's e5-pawn. White may capture exd6 en passant.

steps.explain: The pawn moves to d6 and the d5-pawn disappears. Notation: exd6 (sometimes "e.p." is added).

steps.prompt: You are Black. White just played c2-c4. Capture en passant.
steps.explain: Your d4-pawn takes on c3, the square the white pawn skipped. Black captures en passant from its 4th rank.

steps.question: The black pawn reached d5 earlier, in two single steps. Can White capture it en passant now?
choices: No: en passant only applies right after a two-square move
steps.explain: Here nothing has just double-stepped, so a normal capture on d5 is impossible (the pawn is straight ahead) and en passant does not apply.

steps.question: Black played ...d5, and White replied with a king move instead of capturing. Can White play exd6 on the following move?
steps.explain: En passant must be done immediately or never.

steps.prompt: Black has just played ...d7-d5 with check. Find White's only legal move.
steps.explain: The king cannot move: every square is covered and Kxd5 walks into the defended square. Only en passant removes the checking pawn. Always remember this capture when you list your options.

steps.question: On which rank must a white pawn stand to capture en passant?
steps.explain: White captures e.p. from rank 5; Black from rank 4. These are the only ranks where an enemy double step can land beside your pawn.

steps.question: Retrieval check: which pieces can capture en passant?
choices: Only pawns, and only pawns can be captured that way
steps.explain: It is purely a pawn-takes-pawn rule.

steps.question: Retrieval check: after exd6 e.p., where does the white pawn stand?
steps.explain: On the skipped square, d6, as if the black pawn had stopped there.
